block.wareworks.stacker_crane.tooltip.be: The _aisle_ runs in the direction you look. Connect a _shaft_ to the _bottom_; shafts and cogs at the sides do not connect. A _wrench_ turns it only while the crane is _idle_ and _empty_.
Carries out the controller's _jobs_. Faster _rotation_ moves the crane faster; without rotation or when _overstressed_ it _pauses_ where it is and continues later.
Hold _Right-Click_ on the _value panel_ to set the _mast height_: how many _levels_ the crane reaches.
Shows the _aisle length_, the _mast height_, whether a _controller_ is linked, the current _job_ and the _held items_.
block.wareworks.stacker_crane.tooltip.su: The _dock_ of a _stacker crane_. The crane travels along the _aisle_ of _warehouse rails_ in front of it and _stores_ and _retrieves_ items for the _warehouse controller_ behind it.
block.wareworks.warehouse_controller.too: Place it directly _behind_ a _stacker crane_ while looking at the crane; the _display_ faces you.
Hold _Right-Click_ on the _value panel_ to set the _aisle letter_ used in addresses such as _A-03-07R_.
Shows the _status_, the _aisle size_, the number of _storage locations_, _stations_ and _misaligned_ blocks, the _stored items_, the _crane's job_ and the last _planning result_.

Manages one warehouse _aisle_: it gives the aisle its _letter_, finds its _storage locations_ and _stations_, keeps _count_ of the stored items and _plans_ the _stacker crane's_ jobs. It never moves items itself.
The _opening_ faces you: stand in the _aisle_ and place it into a _rack_ beside the aisle.
Accepts items from _belts_, _funnels_, _chutes_, _hoppers_ and _Mechanical Arms_. The _stacker crane_ carries them to a free _storage location_; automation can only _insert_, never take items out.
A _station_ of a warehouse _aisle_ where items _enter_ the warehouse. It _buffers_ arriving items until a _stacker crane_ stores them.
block.wareworks.warehouse_interface.tool: The _brass port_ faces the clicked _inventory_, such as a _chest_ or _barrel_. Clicked on the side of another _warehouse interface_, it copies that direction; otherwise it faces away from you. Keep the _framed plate_ towards the _aisle_.

Click the _filter slot_ below the arm port with an item to store _only_ that item here. _List_, _attribute_ and _package filters_ all work, and an _empty_ slot accepts _everything_. A filter only restricts _storing_: whatever is already inside can always be _retrieved_, and changing a filter never moves items that are already stored.
Shows its _address_, its _filter_, the _attached inventory_, its _used slots_, the most stored _items_ and the items _reserved_ for a running crane job.
Turns the _inventory_ it faces into an _addressable storage location_ of a warehouse aisle. A _stacker crane_ stores items there and takes them out again.
block.wareworks.warehouse_output.tooltip: The _opening_ faces you: stand in the _aisle_ and place it into a _rack_ beside the aisle.

Click the _filter slot_ with the item to request. It sits on the _top_, the _back_ and both _side_ faces, never in the _aisle opening_, where the crane reaches in. Hold _Right-Click_ on it to set the _amount_, at most one _stack_.
Each _pulse_ requests the filter item from the _warehouse controller_: up to the set _amount_, at most what is _in stock_. The _stacker crane_ then brings the items here; pulse again for more.
Shows its _address_, the _buffered items_, the _pending request_ with the items _delivered_ so far, and why the last request was _refused_.
A _station_ of a warehouse _aisle_ where retrieved items _leave_ the warehouse. _Funnels_, _chutes_, _hoppers_ and _Mechanical Arms_ can pull them out.
block.wareworks.warehouse_production.too: The _opening_ faces you: stand in the _aisle_ and place it into a _rack_ beside the aisle.

_Right-Click_ with an _empty hand_ to open it. Click a _slot_ with an item to set an _ingredient_ or the _result_, and _scroll_ on a slot to change its _amount_. Nothing is used up: the pattern only says what one run of your machine needs and makes.

The _terminal_ marks a pattern's result as _producible_ even when none is in stock. Ordering it reserves the _ingredients_, the crane delivers them here, and the _product_ returns to the warehouse through a _warehouse input_ like any other item.
Shows its _address_, its _patterns_, the running _production orders_ with their _state_ and the _buffered items_.

A _station_ of a warehouse _aisle_ that feeds your _machines_. Define a _pattern_ here, and the _stacker crane_ brings its _ingredients_ to this block; your own _funnel_, _chute_, _belt_ or _Mechanical Arm_ carries them into the machine. Wareworks never crafts anything itself.
block.wareworks.warehouse_rail.tooltip.b: Runs in the direction you look. A _gap_, another block or a rail _across_ the aisle ends the aisle.
block.wareworks.warehouse_rail.tooltip.s: Lays out the _aisle_ of a _stacker crane_. The aisle is as long as the _straight line_ of rails in front of the crane's _dock_.
block.wareworks.warehouse_terminal.toolt: The _screen_ faces you and the _arm port_ the opposite way: stand where you want to read the terminal, with the _aisle_ on the far side of the _rack_. The port then moves to whichever side of the terminal the aisle really is on.
The _wrench_ turns the _screen_ to the next face, never onto the _arm port_: the crane keeps loading the terminal from the _aisle_ while you put the screen where you stand.

The screen lists everything the _aisle_ holds with the amount that is still _available_. Every request is a normal _retrieval job_: the crane brings the items here, just like a request from a _warehouse output_.
Shows its _address_, the _buffered items_, the _pending request_ with the items _delivered_ so far, and why the last request was _refused_.
A _station_ of a warehouse _aisle_ with a _screen_: ask for items here and the _stacker crane_ fetches them. _Funnels_, _chutes_, _hoppers_ and _Mechanical Arms_ can pull them out again.

wareworks.ponder.shared.crane_needs_rota: Stacker Cranes need Rotational Force from below
Moving Items with a Stacker Crane
Stacker Cranes store and retrieve items in a warehouse aisle
The aisle is the straight line of Warehouse Rails in front of the dock
Storage sits on both sides of the aisle, on as many levels as the crane can reach
A Warehouse Controller behind the dock keeps the stock and plans every job
Faster rotation moves it faster; without rotation it pauses where it is
It travels along the rails and lifts its carriage to the right level
Then its telescopic arm reaches into the rack and the grabber moves the items
The Mast Height on the dock sets how many levels the crane can reach
wareworks.ponder.tag.warehouse.descripti: Components which store and retrieve items with Stacker Cranes
wareworks.ponder.warehouse_filters.text_: Every storage location has a filter slot on its aisle side
An empty slot accepts everything, which is how every warehouse starts
Click it with an item, and only that item is stored here
List, attribute and package filters work the same way
Dedicated locations fill before any unfiltered one
Changing a filter moves nothing, and what is inside can always be retrieved
An item that matches no filter needs a location without one
wareworks.ponder.warehouse_interface.tex: Any inventory beside the aisle can become a storage location
A Warehouse Interface in front of it turns it into one
Its brass port faces the inventory, its framed plate with the arm slot faces the aisle
Together with the crane's aisle, every location gets an address: aisle letter, level and position
Goggles show that address, the attached inventory and what it stores
wareworks.ponder.warehouse_production.te: A Warehouse Production feeds the machines you build next to it
Its pattern only says what one run of your machine needs and makes; nothing is used up
A terminal offers that result even when the warehouse holds none of it
The controller reserves the ingredients and the crane brings them to the station
Your own funnel, chute, belt or Mechanical Arm carries them into the machine
Wareworks delivers and collects; it never crafts anything itself
The product comes back through an ordinary Warehouse Input, like any other item
The crane stores it, and your waiting request is served from that stock
wareworks.ponder.warehouse_requesting.te: Right-click the screen with an empty hand to open the terminal
It lists everything the aisle holds, and the search box finds an item by name
Click an item for the amount in the field, Shift for a stack, Ctrl for everything
Clicking the same item again grows the open request instead of starting a second trip
The crane fetches the items from the locations that hold them
and drops them into the terminal's own slots
Funnels, chutes, hoppers and Mechanical Arms can pull them out from there
wareworks.ponder.warehouse_retrieving.te: Items leave a warehouse through a Warehouse Output
Click its filter slot with the item you want
Hold Right-Click on it to set the amount, at most one stack
Every redstone pulse asks the controller for that amount
The crane fetches the items from the location that holds them
and drops them into the output, where funnels, chutes, hoppers and Mechanical Arms pull them out
wareworks.ponder.warehouse_storing.text_: Items enter a warehouse through a Warehouse Input
Belts, funnels, chutes, hoppers and Mechanical Arms can put items in; nothing comes back out
The Warehouse Controller looks for a free storage location and orders a job
The crane drives to the input and its grabber takes the items
It carries them to the chosen location and puts them into the inventory behind it
While free locations are left, every item type gets one of its own
wareworks.ponder.warehouse_terminal.head: Placing a Warehouse Terminal
wareworks.ponder.warehouse_terminal.text: A Warehouse Terminal is placed with its screen facing you
Placed from beside the rack, the controller turns its arm port onto the aisle by itself
Stand where you want to read it: the screen keeps its face, only the port moves
A Wrench turns the screen to the next face, never onto the port, and off the aisle side
Goggles show its address, what was delivered here and why a request was refused
